# Example transcript: running s06.
#
# This is an ILLUSTRATIVE run, not a byte-exact fixture. There is NO LLM call in
# this chapter — the mechanism is the I/O + command layer itself — so this whole
# transcript IS deterministic. The deterministic tests (which DO run in CI) live
# in io_test.go and commands_test.go.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Drive the REPL by piping commands on stdin. Lines starting with "/" are
# slash commands handled locally; anything else is a chat message forwarded to
# the coder stub. The prompt prefix ("diff> ") carries the edit format, exactly
# like upstream get_input (io.py L545-552).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ printf '/help\n/add main.go\n/ls\nplease rename foo to bar\n/drop main.go\n/frobnicate\n/quit\n' | go run .
[s06] interactive shell. Lines starting with / are commands; anything else is a chat message. Try /help, /add, /ls, /quit, or Ctrl-D to exit.
diff> Available commands:
  /add   Add a file to the chat so it can be edited
  /diff  Show a (stubbed) diff of the in-chat files
  /drop  Remove a file from the chat to free context
  /help  List the available commands
  /ls    List repo files and mark which are in the chat

# /add mutates the in-chat file set (upstream cmd_add L799). It NEVER hits the
# network — this is the whole reason commands are intercepted before the coder.
diff> Added main.go to the chat

# /ls now reflects that mutated state: main.go has moved into "Files in chat",
# the rest of the repo universe stays under "not in the chat" (cmd_ls L1064).
diff> Repo files not in the chat:
  README.md
  util.go
Files in chat:
  main.go

# A PLAIN line (no leading "/") is NOT a command, so ParseAndRun returns
# handled=false and the loop forwards it to the coder. The coder stub reports the
# scope it WOULD send (1 file in chat). A real build assembles those files +
# message into a CreateMessageRequest here; s06 stops at the boundary.
diff> [coder] would send to the LLM with 1 file(s) in chat: "please rename foo to bar"

# /drop reverses /add (cmd_drop L912).
diff> Removed main.go from the chat

# An unknown command is reported as an error and is still "handled" — a typo'd
# command is NOT silently sent to the LLM (upstream run L332 / do_run L291-293).
diff> Invalid command: /frobnicate (try /help)

# /quit ends the loop (upstream cmd_exit). Ctrl-D (EOF) does the same.
diff> Bye.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Other things to try:
#   go run . -files a.go,b.go,c.go   # seed a different repo file universe
#   go run . -format whole           # prompt prefix becomes "whole> "
#   go run . -yes                    # auto-answer every confirmation as yes
#   echo "/add nope.go" | go run .   # /add on an unknown file asks to create it
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The deterministic tests (these run in CI, no network):
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
$ go test ./...
ok  	learn-aider/s06	0.3s
